title: Peppermint and cocoa lip scrub
subtitle: A sugar scrub for dry and chapped lips
excerpt: Caster sugar in a cocoa butter and coconut oil base with peppermint essential oil, for gently exfoliating chapped lips. Apply with a fingertip, rub in circles, and rinse. Makes one 15 ml tin; keeps two months.
sourceNotes: Sugar as lip exfoliant: general cosmetic science reference. Peppermint essential oil usage on lips: IFRA guideline for leave-on oral-adjacent products; maximum 0.4% peppermint EO in leave-on products near the mouth; this formula uses a rinse-off product, making the guideline less restrictive. Cocoa butter skin compatibility: CIR safety assessment (open access).

recipe.yieldDescription: 1 tin (~15 ml lip scrub, approximately 20 uses)
recipe.batchNotes: Pours into three 15 ml tins at the same batch; multiply ingredients by three.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make a tin and keep it in a bathroom drawer. Sets in one hour.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Keeps two months in a sealed tin at room temperature. Warm weather may soften the scrub; refrigerate in summer. Discard if the scrub develops an off smell or visible mould; introduced moisture from wet fingers is the most common cause. Always use clean, dry fingers to scoop.

glossaryTerms.definition: Caster or granulated sugar used as a gentle physical exfoliant. Sugar dissolves in contact with moisture, which means it becomes progressively softer and less abrasive as you rub, making it well-suited to the delicate skin of the lips.

that softens and dissolves as you rub, which prevents over-exfoliation on the thin skin of the lips. The cocoa butter and coconut oil leave the lips moisturised after rinsing. The peppermint essential oil adds a cooling tingle and a clean scent.

deodorised; melts slightly above body temperature

content.text: Melt the cocoa butter and coconut oil together over a bain-marie until just liquid. Remove from the heat and let cool to 40°C.
Stir in the caster sugar and the peppermint essential oil. Work quickly as the mixture firms up as it cools.
Pour into the tin immediately. Leave for one hour to firm before sealing.

Scoop a small amount with a clean, dry fingertip. Rub gently over the lips in circular motions for one to two minutes. Rinse with warm water or wipe off with a damp cloth. Apply a lip balm afterwards. Use two to three times per week on chapped lips; once a week for maintenance.
Keeps two months in a sealed tin. Always use a clean, dry finger to scoop. Discard if mould appears or the scrub smells off.
